content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Pittsburgh

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: Verify you meet PMI's education and professional experience requirements for the PMP credential. Most candidates hold a bachelor's degree plus documented project-management experience, or an associate degree with additional hours. Review the full criteria on PMI's website, then contact Granite PM Academy to confirm your qualifications before enrolling.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Our course covers all five process groups and ten knowledge areas tested on the exam. Attend sessions on a schedule that fits your work commitments—whether that's full-time intensive or part-time modules. You'll earn the contact hours required by PMI to sit for the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing the bootcamp, create your PMI account and submit your PMP application, detailing your project-management experience and education. Pay the exam fee directly to PMI. Granite PM Academy's team can guide you through the application portal to ensure accuracy and avoid delays in PMI's approval process.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor office hours—to build confidence before test day. The PMP exam is proctored and computer-delivered; schedule your appointment at a testing center or via remote proctoring. Our instructors remain available to answer final questions as your exam date approaches.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you'll hold the PMP credential for three years. During that cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) by attending training, conferences, or volunteer project-management work. Granite PM Academy offers ongoing PDU-eligible courses to help you stay current and renew your certification when the three-year term ends.
